clusters.change: Probe results are named docs/probes/<sbx version>/<id>-<host>.json; 11 11.4 gains a 'stale' transition fired by a floor or pin change; the 12 12.1 pin table gains a column 'on bump' naming the probes to re-run and the recordings to re-record.
clusters.cost: A naming change, one lifecycle row, one column.
clusters.resolution_text: A column in the existing pin table instead of a new 11.5 table.

clusters.title: The v3 descriptor grammar is parsed by internal/oci and internal/render with no single owner, and nothing says what happens when sbx adds a capability type the strict grammar refuses.
clusters.scenario: sbx adds a capability type; every sync fails closed until a release; the release teaches oci and forgets render; I28 holds for one parser.
clusters.change: 12 12.2, oci row: 'owns the descriptor grammar and the normalized capability set; render imports them'. Index, Deferred decisions: a row 'a capability type sbx adds after v1', holding fail closed, reopened by the first sync that fails on an unmodeled type, cost one release.
clusters.cost: A cell, a sentence in 01 1.4 and 06 6.1, one deferred row.
clusters.resolution_text: oci as the one owner; no new package.

clusters.title: The package tree, the module map and S9's coverage list are three hand lists with different names for the same code.
clusters.scenario: A package is renamed; the three lists change in different PRs; tools/ci coverage measures a package that no longer exists.
clusters.change: 12 12.2: 'Each module id names its directories in a column of this table; a test of tools/ci holds 02 2.1's tree and S9's list to those directories.'
clusters.cost: One column and one test.
clusters.resolution_text: A consistency test, not a generator.

clusters.title: The pin file read by four consumers is in no tree and has no writer for the workload entry; three formats have no schema although 03 says each has one; the I4, I25 and I8 guards live in packages outside every ask-first surface, so mutate does not run on a PR that changes only them.
clusters.scenario: The pin file is hand-edited for the workload digest; a change to sbxdrv's argv builders merges without mutation testing although I4 lives there.
clusters.change: 02 2.1: add the pin file with its writer (julieta pin workload). 03 opening: name dora.v1, ledger-entry/v1 and the view files as exempt from the schema rule, or 02 2.1 lists their schemas. 10 10.2, mutate row: it also runs on any PR touching a file that holds a guard tagged for an invariant.
clusters.cost: Three sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Exempt by name rather than add three schemas while R8-12-8 and R8-12-9 may defer two of the formats; mutate keyed on guard tags, not a new surface.

clusters.title: The build order brings the product to real sbx only at the release candidate, while 10 10.3 lists what the fake cannot model, so each real-host failure costs a new candidate and a new block B.
clusters.scenario: 91 tasks pass against the fake; the first real run finds a mount or policy argv that differs; each fix outside docs/ needs a new candidate and about 90 minutes of block B per host.
clusters.change: 12 12.2, build order: two real-host smoke steps that are not block B results - after the sync slice (init, sync, approve on one host) and after run (J1 to J3 on one host, from a dry-run build of main) - each one host-suite command whose output is pasted under Evidence and not committed under docs/probes/. Replace the 'Residual rework risk' sentence by what these runs cover.
clusters.cost: Two short maintainer sittings and a host-suite selector.
clusters.resolution_text: Recommendation: accept; two sittings are cheaper than one extra block B.
clusters.operator_reason: Adds maintainer sittings to the build order; only the maintainer commits the maintainer's time.

clusters.title: The spec mandates a plan and fixes its order but has no re-plan rule, and the plan's counts and dependencies are kept by hand.
clusters.scenario: With 3 of 102 tasks merged, plan.md already says seven decision records (there are eight) and 28 rows (there are 36).
clusters.change: 12 12.2: 'A PR that changes a spec section updates the plan tasks that implement it in the same PR. tools/ci sequences checks plan.md: task ids are contiguous, each Depends on names an existing lower id or block, each Implements cites an existing section. The plan states no counts.'
clusters.cost: One rule and one sequences extension.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed.

clusters.title: Guides and the README are written in the docs module after block B, so every guide's expected output is typed after the only real-host run, in text blocks no check compares.
clusters.scenario: The J1 guide shows the gate 2 summary as the writer remembers it; the real first line differs; no host runs again.
clusters.change: 12 12.2, build order: the guides and the README text of the docs module land before the release candidate, so block B runs each guide as written; after block B the docs module only adds ADRs. The recorder-based check is not added.
clusters.cost: A reorder of the build order (the plan moves T094).
clusters.resolution_text: The reorder only.

clusters.title: dora runs tokenless as the last step of release.yml and backfills the whole history, and the spec does not say what a 403 or 429 does to --attach or the release.
clusters.scenario: History grows past anonymous limits; dora --attach fails; the release run ends red after the release is published.
clusters.change: 12 12.10: 'A rate-limit or auth error exits with its own code; a failed --attach leaves the release published and the run red, and re-running the step attaches the file. The tool paginates and sends the API version header.'
clusters.cost: Three sentences and a fixture row.
clusters.resolution_text: Applies only if R8-12-9 keeps the tool in v1; otherwise it moves with the tool.

clusters.title: Change fail rate and rework count rely on Fixes-release trailers that authors must remember, which is mechanical memory.
clusters.scenario: An agent fixes a release bug without the trailer; nobody adds it; instability reads zero.
clusters.change: 12 12.4, pr row: 'after the first deployment, a pull request with a fix commit carries a Fixes-release trailer or the line Fixes-release: none'.
clusters.cost: One pr clause and its fixtures.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply; it holds whether or not R8-12-9 defers the tool, since the trailer data cannot be backfilled.

clusters.title: maintainerWaitSeconds mixes agent and outside PRs in one median, so the stranger's wait is hidden.
clusters.scenario: Agent PRs merge in an hour while outside PRs wait a month; the median looks healthy and the deferred merge-checkpoint decision reads it.
clusters.change: 12 12.10: 'The maintainer wait mixes the operator's own pull requests and outside ones; the split waits for the first outside pull request.'
clusters.cost: One sentence.
clusters.resolution_text: State as a limit; the split is deferred to its trigger.
